title: Cells, execution order, and the notebook that only works out of order

videos.script: Run a cell. Run it again. Same code. {{same-code}} A different answer. Nothing is broken. The kernel remembered what the first run did. {{remembered}} That is the whole lesson in one move. A notebook page is a record of what happened. The kernel is what is true now. {{record}} Most of the time they agree. This lesson is about the times they do not. {{disagree}} A cell that ran before the one above it. A variable whose cell was deleted, still alive in memory. {{orphan}} A module edited on disk, and a kernel still using the old one. {{module}} None of these raise an error. Each one works for the person who made it, and fails for the next person. {{next-person}} The cure is one menu item. Restart the kernel, and run every cell from the top. {{restart}} If the answers survive that, the notebook is a document. If they do not, you found out first. {{end}}
